questions.text: Why keep a short pre-roll audio buffer before voice activity detection triggers a new turn?

options.A: To include the assistant’s previous answer in the user transcript.
options.B: To wait for the entire utterance before starting audio capture.
options.C: To recover speech onset that occurred before the detector triggered.
options.D: To replace the speech recognizer with a fixed-length recording.

questions.explanation: Pre-roll retains recent audio from before the trigger so detection delay does not clip the first sounds or words.

questions.text: On user interruption, playback stops, but the old LLM continues generating and fills the next response queue. What should the interruption handler also do?

options.A: Cancel the old LLM generation and discard its queued output.
options.B: Increase the silence threshold before recognizing the interruption.
options.C: Append the old generated text to the new user transcript.
options.D: Restart playback when the old model finishes generating.

questions.explanation: Barge-in must cancel stale generation and prevent its buffered output from leaking into the new turn.

questions.text: In capture_turn, each silent chunk after speech increments silent by 20; a speech chunk resets silent to 0. With silence_ms = 60, after speech then two silent chunks, one speech chunk, and two silent chunks, has it returned?

options.A: Yes, because four silent chunks exceed 60 ms in total.
options.B: Yes, because any silent chunk immediately ends the turn.
options.C: No, because the silence counter increases only during speech.
options.D: No, because the latest speech reset the consecutive silence counter.

questions.explanation: The intervening speech resets silent to zero. The final two silent chunks accumulate only 40 ms, below the 60 ms threshold.
